script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 2. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Newton said gravity is a force that pulls objects together.  Then Einstein came along and said: there is no force.  Objects just follow straight paths through curved space.

Imagine placing a bowling ball on a stretched rubber sheet. The sheet curves around it. A marble rolled nearby follows that curve toward the bowling ball. That's gravity—not a force, but geometry. Mass tells space how to curve; space tells mass how to move. Right now, you're in free fall toward Earth's center.  You don't feel it because the ground pushes up against you.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: What feels like external force might be the shape of the system you're in.  Before blaming the pull, examine the curvature.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Gravity Awareness - Feel the Fall.

Here's your activity: Drop something small and watch it fall. Now imagine: it's not being pulled down—it's following a curved path through space-time, and the ground is rushing up to meet it. How does this reframe change the experience? This helps you experience gravity with new understanding.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what gravity actually does can be applied to gravity awareness - feel the fall. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
